page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1.medium is a compute-optimized virtual instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The allocation provides two dedicated virtual CPUs derived from a single physical core with two threads per core. Memory capacity is provisioned at 4.0 GB, establishing a standard compute-oriented ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Cache hierarchy consists of 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache, with instruction set support including AVX, AVX-512F, and AES cryptographic acceleration. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local instance storage, and network bandwidth operates at a baseline of 0 Gbps.

Performance across synthetic and application benchmarks reflects its small core footprint. In CPU testing, the system achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 913.0 and a multi-core score of 1064.0, alongside a PassMark CPU mark of 1824.84. Stress-ng scores show 1097.68 on single-core runs and 1455.38 under multi-threaded execution. Memory bandwidth tests measure cached reads at 81.52 GB/sec, while uncached large-block reads and writes settle at 10.27 GB/sec and 9.34 GB/sec respectively. Application-level tests demonstrate Redis throughput of 1.42 million SET operations per second and static web serving capacity of 1.25 GB/sec, alongside a 36.38 tokens/sec generation rate for lightweight 135M-parameter language models.

Given its minimal footprint of one physical core and modest RAM capacity, the server offers an economical entry tier within dedicated compute classes. The trade-off centers on constrained parallel throughput and the total reliance on remote network-attached volumes for persistent data storage. Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1.medium is best aligned with low-concurrency operations, including simple web endpoints, non-intensive microservices, utility tasks, continuous integration workers, and light database caching layers.
